holes_found.description: SENTENCE-5 RHETORICAL OVER-CLOSURE ("neither reflects any physical signal"). The newly hardened sentence reads: "The claim that 'ellipse never lost across V5–V9' is therefore either trivial within each version or, since the city-pair dataset expanded across versions, an artifact of the growing dataset — neither case is evidence of physical geometry, and neither reflects any physical signal." The two-case dichotomy (within-version-trivial vs cross-version-dataset-artifact) is correct, but the closing clause "neither reflects any physical signal" reads as if the two cases exhaust the possibilities. A determined defender could reply: "Your two cases don't exhaust the joint space. A genuine physical ellipticity would still show up even under dataset expansion — the residual pattern could reflect both curve-fit slack AND a real geometric signal." The stronger correct framing is that the ellipse-never-lost claim does not *evidence* a physical signal (rather than that the residual does not *reflect* one), because absence of evidence is not evidence of absence at the sentence level. This is a rhetorical polish issue, not a load-bearing weakness — the b/a-wander evidence (sentence 11, 29% variation) and the WGS84-vs-dome magnitude gap (sentence 12) do the actual work of ruling out a real physical geometric signal. Severity: minor per curmudgeon TLDR-imprecision-not-misleading standard, applied to prose imprecision that does not mislead once the paragraph is read as a whole.
holes_found.recommendation: Optional single-word softening: change "neither reflects any physical signal" to "neither evidences a physical geometric signal" or delete the trailing clause entirely — the preceding "neither case is evidence of physical geometry" already carries the load without the redundant/stronger second clause. Do not block on this; the argument survives fine as-is once the reader continues to sentence 11.

holes_found.description: IN-TEXT DATASET-EXPANSION CLAIM WOULD BENEFIT FROM A SOURCE HOOK. Sentence 5's new phrasing asserts "the city-pair dataset expanded across versions" as a factual claim in the body prose. This claim is factually correct (raw-text/04-coordinates.txt line 18 says "was ~40% in V9" implying a smaller/different V9 city set, line 80 has a "=== WHAT CHANGED V9 -> V50.6 ===" heading), but the current text carries no in-line citation — a reader who doubts the dataset expansion has nothing to click. Since we criticize the dome for making unbacked assertions (48.6% RMS), we should be careful not to introduce a symmetric weak spot in our own text. This is not a factual error, and the source is public dome text, so the impact is bounded. Severity: minor.
holes_found.recommendation: Optional: add a link. Suggested minimal edit: change "since the city-pair dataset expanded across versions" to "since the city-pair dataset expanded across versions (per the dome's own raw-text/04-coordinates.txt V9→V50.6 change log)" or link to the dome-site coordinates page anchor if one exists. kernel_of_truth.description: The dome model has correctly identified (data/wins.json:030.detail_evidence sentence 6) that inter-city distances measured on a sphere and projected onto a flat azimuthal-equidistant disc exhibit systematic latitude-dependent residuals. The dome's observation that a 2-parameter shape (ellipse) fits these residuals with smaller error than a 1-parameter shape (circle) is genuinely true, and is the same observation any cartographer flattening a sphere would make. raw-text/06-evolution.txt confirms internal awareness that the model "was always operating in WGS84 space" — the dome does know its distances come from WGS84 coordinates.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The kernel of truth is a cartographic observation about projection distortion, not a physical claim about disc shape. Three converging arguments defeat the physical-disc-shape interpretation, all present in the c6 text: (1) The nested-model structure (data/wins.json:030.detail_evidence sentence 4, hardened by ISS-3004) means an ellipse fit cannot lose to a circle fit on the same version's data; the cross-version version is trivialized by dataset expansion (data/wins.json:030.detail_evidence sentence 5). (2) The parameter oscillation (b/a 0.70→0.90 across V5-V9, ~29% variance, raw-text/04-coordinates.txt line 33) is the empirical signature of curve-fitting to a growing dataset, not iterative measurement convergence — real geodetic refinements (raw-text/05-model.txt WGS84 b/a=0.997) move in the 6th-7th decimal, not the first (data/wins.json:030.detail_evidence sentences 11–13). (3) The dome's own OPEN-003 admits ellipse parameters still converging (raw-text/05-model.txt line 97; data/wins.json:030.detail_evidence sentence 14) — a fitted-parameter admission from the model itself. A fourth argument (60× magnitude disproportion vs WGS84, stronger_arguments #1 above) remains available for promotion but is not yet in the text.

The post-hoc rationale is now WIN-030-specific and does not depend on inapplicable monitor-script boilerplate; the tldr_verdict now covers both AIC/BIC and post-hoc prongs. The BEST remaining defense a fair-minded dome defender could construct in July 2026: "Your sentence-5 two-case dichotomy is presented as exhaustive, but it isn't — a real physical ellipticity would still show up in the residual even under dataset expansion. The dichotomy proves neither case *individually* evidences physical signal, not that no evidence exists." This is the hole #1 finding above; it is a rhetorical polish issue, not a substantive attack. The rebuttal is trivial ("the b/a-wander evidence at sentence 11 and WGS84-magnitude gap at sentence 12 do the actual signal-elimination work; sentence 5 is scaffolding"). Secondary defense: the c6 text asserts "city-pair dataset expanded across versions" without an in-line citation (hole #2 above) — a defender could ask "where does that claim come from?" — but the source is public dome text so this is a rhetorical polish issue not a substantive one.
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Neither remaining defense justifies a patch on its own — both are single-word polish edits at most. Recommend closing the c5→c6 verify loop as SUCCESSFUL: the c5 defense_survives=3 posture is materially reduced to defense_survives=1, no substantive attacks remain, and the two minor holes above are optional polish.
